text:
Asha: Sundown handoff — handing primary to Miguel. Quick recap of the last 6h: we saw recurring latency spikes and intermittent 504s for inference requests originating from eu-west. Root cause appears to be KV cache slot thrash after a memory pressure event on the local shard pool.
Miguel: Got it, taking primary. Any customer impact right now?
Asha: Impact was ~3% of requests showing p95 latency spikes to ~1.2s and a 504 rate bump to ~0.6% for ~45m window. Most traffic routed to fallback model and clients seeing degraded latency, not complete failures. We mitigated with temporary routing rule to increase fallback capacity and applied backpressure on batcher; error budget held.
Priya: Which services are involved? Is this the runtime kvcache or the redis-tier?
Asha: It's runtime-level KV cache inside the serving runtime (local shard), not central redis. The shard eviction loop got stuck because of a small regression in the allocator path after the tokenizer lib upgrade on 2026-03-02.
pagerduty-bot: Incident PAGER: INF-KV-THRASH triggered at 2026-03-12T19:03:12Z — severity: S2 — paging: Asha (primary).
Tom: Any config toggles we used to stabilize?
Asha: Yes — applied two mitigation steps: 1) disabled the new tokenizer mempool feature (config: runtime.features.tokenizer_mempool=false) 2) lowered batcher.max_concurrent_batches from 32 -> 16. Both were rolled via canary at 19:12 and global at 19:28. Latency returned to baseline within ~8m of global flip.
deploy-bot: deploy/infra-runtime v4.7.2 -> v4.7.1 rollback initiated by @Asha at 2026-03-12T19:28:02Z — status: success
Miguel: Where's the runbook pointer for this exact scenario? I want the steps in case it reoccurs during my shift.
Asha: Runbook: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OPS/pages/kv-cache-eviction-runbook — follow sections 'Immediate mitigations' and 'Rollbacks'. Short checklist I used:
```
- Check shard-memory usage: /infra/metrics/dashboard?panel=kvcache_shard_mem
- If shard mem high and evictions stalled: set runtime.features.tokenizer_mempool=false
- Reduce batcher concurrency: batcher.max_concurrent_batches=16
- If not improving within 10m: roll runtime to previous patch (v4.7.2 -> v4.7.1)
- Notify routing to route traffic to fallback model pool
```
Priya: Thanks. Any outstanding work for tomorrow?
Asha: Action items tracked in the incident epic: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4281 — TL;DR: revert tokenizer allocator fix and add stronger eviction metrics / alerting. I opened a PR to add eviction-stall alert (PR #5892).
Miguel: I'll own pager coverage from 19:30->03:30. Primary: Miguel, Secondary: Priya. Tom is backup for infra escalations.
Tom: I'll watch the infra dashboards and check the node-level oom logs if we see any more memory anomalies. Command for quick checks:
```bash
kubectl -n runtime get pods -l app=redwood-runtime
kubectl -n runtime logs <pod> -c runtime --since=30m | rg "eviction|mempool|OOM" -n
```
Asha: Current status: stable, rollback done, routing fallback removed (rebalanced at 20:05). Postmortem window open; please don't delete any logs until postmortem closes.
Miguel: Thanks, noted. I'll run a light synthetic against eu-west every 30m and ping here if any regression. What thresholds do we want to auto-escalate on?
Priya: Escalation thresholds: p95 > 900ms for 10m OR 504% > 0.5% for 5m. Those are in the runbook alert section — I left a note to tighten p99 too.
infra-bot: Alert rule updated: INF-KV-THRASH -> p95>900ms 10m, 504_rate>0.5% 5m (by Priya).
Miguel: Asha — anything else I should know about customer-facing comms? Did Support open any tickets?
Asha: Support opened 2 tickets related to a small SaaS customer noticing degraded latency; no major outages. I added context to both tickets and flagged them for follow-up after postmortem.
Tom: I'll keep an eye on eviction_count and add ephemeral logs to the incident epic. If we see >3 eviction-stalls in an hour, page me immediately.
Miguel: OK taking over. If things look healthy at 23:00 I'll hand to Priya for overnight. Thanks @Asha for the handoff. :thumbsup:
Asha: Thanks — feel free to DM if you need any quick context. Good luck and ping on-call if anything spikes.
Priya: Acknowledged. I'll be secondary and on-call coverage handoff at 23:00 if needed.
deploy-bot: Reminder: next runtime canary scheduled at 2026-03-13T02:00:00Z for v4.7.3 — Miguel, please approve or pause if still unstable.
Miguel: Noted — I'll pause the canary if we see any regression in the evening checks.
infra-bot: Thread archived by infra-bot after 2h inactivity (automated).
